item.title: Nigeria’s unity must rise above ethnic, regional divisions – Sultan
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, has challenged Nigerian Muslims to rise above ethnic, regional and social divisions and take greater responsibility for safeguarding national unity, promoting religious tolerance and confronting the security challenges threatening the country. The revered monarch warned that ethnicity, regional affiliations and differences in social backgrounds must never be allowed to undermine the unity of the Muslim Ummah or the collective responsibility of Nigerians to build a peaceful, stable and prosperous nation. He stressed that Muslims, irrespective of their ethnic origins or geographical locations, shared a common religious identity and must demonstrate, through their conduct and relationships, the unifying principles of Islam. The Sultan made the call on Sunday in Ibadan, Oyo State, while addressing participants at the 11th General Assembly of the Muslim Ummah of South-West Nigeria (MUSWEN), held at the M.O. Abdul Hall, University of Ibadan Central Mosque Auditorium. The assembly, which attracted Islamic leaders, traditional rulers, government representatives and other dignitaries, was held under the theme, “Insecurity in Nigeria: A Technology-Driven and Collective Approach for National Development.” Abubakar, who is also the President-General of the Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA), maintained that the survival and progress of the Muslim community depended largely on its ability to preserve its common identity and resist divisive tendencies capable of weakening its collective strength. According to him, the Almighty Allah created humanity as one family, making it imperative for Muslims to place their religious obligations and shared humanity above ethnic sentiments and other considerations. “We are one big family. Ethnicity should never be a determining factor in identifying who is a Muslim and who is not. Almighty Allah created us as one human family and commanded us to worship Him alone and glorify His name,” the Sultan said. He insisted that Islam must remain the guiding principle of Muslims’ lives, urging them not to allow political, ethnic or regional interests to displace the fundamental teachings of their faith. “It must be Islam first, Islam first, Islam first, and Islam last,” he declared. The Sultan further noted the equality of all human beings before Allah, explaining that neither ethnic background, social standing nor material possessions determined an individual’s worth in the sight of God. He said righteousness, piety and the fear of Allah remained the true standards by which human beings should be judged. “Before Allah, we are all equal. The best among us is the one who possesses the greatest degree of piety and righteousness,” he said. item.title: 2027 Grammys Nominations To Be Announced Monday
item.description: Nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, scheduled to hold in February 2027, will be announced on Monday, November 16, with Nigerian music fans able to follow the presentation from 1:45 p.m. West African Time (WAT). The Recording Academy will unveil nominees across all 100 categories during a special presentation led by its Chief Executive Officer, Harvey Mason Jr., and Chair of its Board of Trustees, Dr Chelsey Green. The announcement will begin at 7:45 a.m. Eastern Time (1:45 p.m. WAT), while the complete list of nominees is expected to be published around 9 a.m. Eastern Time (3 p.m. WAT). The presentation will be streamed live on Grammy.com and the official Grammys YouTube channel, with additional coverage on ABC’s Good Morning America. Grammys For the first time, the nominations presentation will also be broadcast live at The Square in Times Square, New York, in partnership with Hilton, the Recording Academy’s official hotel partner. Several Grammy-winning and nominated artistes are expected to join Mason and Green in announcing the nominees. They include Alan Menken, Amy Allen, Carly Pearce, David Guetta, FYÜTCH and Aura V, Herbie Hancock, Israel Houghton, Juanes, Kehlani, Linda Perry, Meghan Foley and Michelle Holme, Olivia Dean, Pharrell Williams, Renée Fleming, YUNGBLUD and Ziggy Marley. New Categories The 2027 edition introduces five new award categories, bringing the total number of categories to 100. They are Best Asian Pop Music Performance, Best Latin Song, Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance, and Best Traditional Folk Album. The eligibility period for the awards covers recordings released between August 31, 2025, and August 28, 2026. LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – FEBRUARY 01: (FOR EDITORIAL USE ONLY) Olivia Dean attends the 68th GRAMMY Awards at Crypto.com Arena on February 01, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. item.title: 2027: Atiku storms Bauchi communities, questions Tinubu’s grassroots outreach
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar weekend took his presidential campaign to communities across Bauchi State, drawing large crowds along his route from the airport to the Bauchi State Presidential Lodge and during a road trip to Azare. The tour, which featured a campaign rally, visits to four communities and courtesy calls on two traditional rulers, was part of his efforts to deepen grassroots engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections, while challenging President Bola Tinubu’s record of direct engagement with Nigerians. Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, said Atiku began the day’s engagements at 8am with consultations with stakeholders before proceeding to an 11am rally in Bauchi. Atiku thanked residents for the reception, saying it had strengthened his resolve to take his message of affordable living and responsible leadership to communities across the country. After the rally, his campaign train travelled by road to Azare, stopping in Soro, Kari, Darazo and Misau, where residents turned out to welcome him and his entourage. In Misau, Atiku paid a courtesy visit to the Emir, Alhaji Ahmed Suleiman, thanking him and his council for their hospitality and words of encouragement. He also acknowledged residents who waited to receive his entourage despite its arrival at nightfall. He arrived in Azare at 10.30pm, where he paid a courtesy visit to the Emir of Katagum, extending his engagements with traditional rulers and community leaders. The campaign team is expected to proceed to Potiskum on Sunday for another rally. However, the ADC campaign used the reported scale of the reception to question Tinubu’s grassroots engagement, challenging the President to demonstrate a similar willingness to meet Nigerians directly. “The scale of yesterday’s welcome raises a simple question: can the sitting President volunteer to meet the people and make even half the effort Atiku has made to reach them?” Shaibu said. item.title: US flight disruptions: Trump admin says air travel chaos may last another day
item.description: The Trump administration said Sunday the air travel havoc triggered by a no-takeoff order could drag on for another day, pushing back its timetable for a return to normal. Hundreds more flights were cancelled and questions remained over how such chaos could unfold in the world’s largest economy, a country that prides itself on its technological prowess. Officials blame Friday’s huge snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables. President Donald Trump on Sunday ended uncharacteristic days of silence on the ground stop, but only to blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the debacle. Trump insisted he inherited a mess from the Biden administration and said Congress, which his party has controlled for two years, must approve funds to upgrade America’s outdated air traffic control system. “The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump said, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration. “Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began,” Trump asserted. FAA chief Bryan Bedford had said Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans stranded at airports would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday. But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday morning it will actually take longer to get planes, crews and travelers to where they need to be. “So, in the airspace, we’re going to see things come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow,” Duffy said on ABC News. “We had airplanes and crews out of position because of Friday, so it takes a little bit of time to do that.” – ‘I’m the secretary’ – Duffy also flatly rejected calls for his resignation over the travel chaos, insisting he inherited woefully outdated air traffic control infrastructure, such as, he said, radar equipment that dates back to the 1960s. “So when we do work and things go wrong, of course I’m the secretary. But I also have to acknowledge what was delivered to me,” Duffy said in an interview on CNN. As of Sunday morning 1,460 flights within, into or out of the United States had been cancelled, according to the travel monitor site flightaware.com. The Trump administration has blamed Friday’s ground stop — meaning no planes can take off — on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines. Friday’s disruption was only the second time such a ground stop had been issued in US airspace, which is among the busiest in the world, since the 9/11 attacks. The ground stop not only plunged US air travel into chaos, it also raised serious concerns about the country’s aging infrastructure. Duffy has appealed for $50 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the air traffic control system, and called for Congress, which controls the purse strings of the US government, to “meet this moment.” But Democrats quickly pounced to say Congress under Trump’s Republicans could already have done this. item.title: Guinea deports 1,557 West Africans in gold mining crackdown
item.description: By Favour Ulebor & Agency Reports Guinea has expelled 1,557 West African nationals arrested and convicted for illegal gold mining as the government intensifies its crackdown on unauthorised mining activities across the country. Judicial and security sources told AFP on Sunday that the foreigners, mostly from Burkina Faso and Mali, were arrested at different mining sites during an operation against illegal mining. The deportees were transported in a convoy of 44 vehicles, which arrived in Kouremale, a border town between Guinea and Mali, on Saturday after leaving the capital, Conakry, on Friday. According to the sources, the foreigners were released and expelled after receiving prison sentences ranging from 18 months to two years. The Guinean government has increased operations against illegal gold mining since the beginning of November, particularly in Siguiri, a major gold-producing region in the northeastern part of the country. Authorities said the crackdown was aimed at stopping the illegal exploitation of mineral resources and reducing the environmental damage caused by unregulated mining. The operations have also affected thousands of West African migrants who travelled to Guinea in search of employment and better living conditions after fleeing poverty and insecurity in their home countries. Meanwhile, the crackdown has sparked tensions between miners and security forces. At least 10 people were killed on Wednesday following violent clashes between miners and security personnel in Siguiri, according to a government statement issued on Thursday. Reacting to the deaths, Guinea’s main opposition coalition on Saturday condemned what it described as an “authoritarian drift” and criticised the government’s use of force “as a method of government.” The latest expulsions come amid growing concerns over the treatment of migrant miners and the government’s efforts to control illegal mining activities. item.title: Adeleke demotes Osun traditional rulers over pro APC stance
item.description: By Shina Abubakar Osogbo The Governor Ademola Adeleke-led administration in Osun State has demoted two traditional rulers, the Alagunbeelewo of Agunbeelewo and the Olu of Irepodun, in Osogbo, the State capital. The demotion of the part 2 traditional rulers was contained in a letter by the Ministry of Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, dated November 5, signed for the Permanent Secretary by one Wale Alliyu and copied the Ataoja of Osogbo. The two separate letters addressed to the affected monarchs, stated that the State Executive Council presided over by the Governor on October 23rd has approved their de-recognise their stools as part 2 traditional rulers back to that minor chieftaincy. “I am directed to inform you that the State Executive Council ably led by His Excellency Senator Ademola Jackson Nurudeen Adeleke has approved the de-recognition of your stool as Part II (Recognized) stool under the Chief’s Law (Cap, 25) Laws of Osun State, 2002 with effect from 23rd October, 2026. “By this de-recognition, your stool now reverts to a Minor Chieftaincy to which Part III of the Chief’s Law applies and consequently, all the rights, privileges and allowances being enjoyed as a recognized Chief will by this development cease. Although the letter did not state any reason for the demotion but the Alagunbeelewo of Agunbeelewo, Chief Maruf Olayiwola disclosed that they were both alleged of associating with the APC instead of the Accord party in the state. “It is unfortunate that till now, no one disclosed our offence but we were told that we are not associating with Accord party and we did not collect money from anyone. We have friends in the APC and cannot deny our relationship with them. I believe that is not enough reason to sack us from the stool. “Governor Adeleke should not allow some persons to reduce the office of the Governor to that of settling personal grudges for the sake of posterity”, he said. Meanwhile, a civil society organisation, Local Government Development Initiative (LGDI), berated the State Government for acting lawless over the matter. Its Spokesperson Adeniyi Faith while addressing newsmen in Osogbo on Sunday, counselled the State Government not to politicise traditional institutions in the state to ensure its sanctity. “We wish to remind Governor Adeleke that the power of a state government over traditional institutions is not unlimited. Such powers must be exercised strictly in accordance with the applicable laws, established procedures, principles of natural justice and the constitutional guarantee of fair hearing. “The government must demonstrate the legal authority, procedural compliance and legitimate grounds for every decision it takes concerning the appointment, suspension or removal of a traditional ruler. Political authority must never be mistaken for unlimited authority. “We are not suggesting that traditional rulers are above the law or cannot be removed under any circumstances. item.title: Bloody Spit: Ghana Waste Dump Poses Health, Environmental ‘Crisis’
item.description: An acrid haze hung over a sprawling dump in Ghana’s capital, Accra, as excavators gouged into mounds of smouldering rubbish. Thin plumes of black smoke curled from burning plastic and rubber, mingling with the rank odour of stagnant lagoon water. At Agbogbloshie, a district on the Korle Lagoon delta, thousands of tonnes of refuse have accumulated over decades, overwhelming the fragile wetlands overlooking a slum of around 80,000 residents, many of them migrants and traders. For scrap dealer James Hassan, a 31-year-old Liberian immigrant, it is both his home and livelihood. Without gloves or a mask, he sifts daily through piles of unwanted electronics and metal for scraps to sell. The skin on his palms is thickened and scarred from cuts and rashes but he has become accustomed to the pain and discomfort. “I have headaches and coughs after long days under the sun, but I have never sought medical care. I feel they are normal,” he told AFP. Environmental health experts say that workers are exposed to toxic metals and chemicals through skin cuts, inhaling waste smoke and dust. Waste collectors dig through piles of waste at the Agbogbloshie dumpsite in Accra, on September 28, 2026. Photo by NIPAH DENNIS / AFP While no study as yet links specific diseases to Agbogbloshie’s pollution, “the cumulative contamination raises concern even if precise causal chains remain unquantified,” epidemiologist Reginald Quansah, of the University of Ghana, said. Global Pipeline Of Waste Waste management is a prominent theme at the COP31 climate talks, which began in Turkey on Monday. Agbogbloshie’s refuse comes largely from beyond Ghana’s borders. Accra’s huge second-hand clothing market has imports from Europe, North America and Asia — but often with a troubling byproduct. “A lot of clothes that are shipped into Ghana come as waste,” Greenpeace Africa’s head of investigations Samuel Quashie-Idun told AFP. Greenpeace estimates that 15 million used garments arrive in Ghana each week. Even after traders extract what they can sell, roughly half ends up as “dead waste” dumped on beaches and fields or burned, it said. One study Greenpeace cited put Ghana’s used clothing imports at over 110,000 tonnes in 2022. For the country’s 35 million people, “these volumes far exceed local demand and… burdens waste systems,” Quashie-Idun said. Greenpeace found that 89 percent of sampled “dead” garments contained petrochemical fibres such as polyester, which shed microplastics as they decay, and release carcinogens hundreds of times above safe levels in smoke when the textiles are burned. “This is not just an environmental crisis… it’s also a human health crisis,” said Hellen Kahaso Dena, Greenpeace’s plastics project expert. ‘Fashion Waste Dumping Ground’ “The global north is effectively using Ghana as a dumping ground for fashion waste,” she told AFP. item.title: Nasarawa 2027: Adamu unveils plans for security, jobs, roads, electricity
item.description: The Social Democratic Party (SDP) governorship candidate in Nasarawa State, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has unveiled plans to improve security, agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment if elected governor in 2027. Adamu outlined his priorities in a five-minute campaign video, saying his experience as a police officer and former Inspector-General of Police had prepared him to serve the state. He said he would bring the same commitment to protecting lives that guided his over three decades in the Nigeria Police Force to governing Nasarawa. “For over three decades, I served Nigeria as a police officer and as your Inspector-General of Police. My duty was to protect lives. Today, I bring that same duty to Nasarawa State to serve as your governor,” he said. The former police chief said he had travelled across the state’s local government areas and wards, where he observed challenges facing farmers, rural communities and public institutions. He listed poor roads, inadequate hospital and school facilities, limited access to clean water and unreliable electricity among the problems requiring urgent attention. Outlining his security plans, Adamu said an SDP administration would build security structures from the ward level to strengthen protection across communities. On agriculture, he promised to provide farmers with tractors and other support, while prioritising the construction and maintenance of roads, particularly in rural areas. “We will put tractors in the hands of our farmers, and this time we will not just promise roads; we will build them and maintain them, reaching the rural communities that have been left behind for too long,” he said. Adamu also pledged to improve education through investment in teachers, modern classrooms and digital learning tools. He said his administration would work with communities at the ward level to improve academic performance. On youth employment, the SDP candidate said existing skill acquisition centres would be linked to employers and start-up support to ensure that graduates could secure jobs or establish businesses. “So, training turns into livelihood, not just a certificate,” he said. He also promised to strengthen the state water board and expand existing water infrastructure to connect more homes and farms to reliable supplies. Adamu promises to complete Farin-Ruwa dam The former IGP identified the completion of the Farin-Ruwa dam in Wamba Local Government Area as a priority, lamenting that the project had remained unfinished for more than 20 years. He said completing the dam would help generate electricity for homes, schools and industries across the state. Adamu further promised to deploy digital technology to monitor government projects and public spending, saying the approach would promote transparency and accountability. item.title: Meet African countries home to some of the world’s oldest universities
item.description: Africa is home to some of the world’s oldest centres of higher learning, with educational institutions that began centuries before many of the universities commonly associated with Europe’s academic history. From Islamic centres of scholarship in North Africa to historic institutions in West Africa, the continent has a long tradition of organised education, research and intellectual development. Some of these institutions started as mosques and religious schools before evolving into universities, while others emerged as colleges during the 19th century. Here are six African countries home to some of the world’s oldest universities and higher-learning institutions. 1. Tunisia – Ez-Zitouna University (737 AD) Tunisia is home to Ez-Zitouna University, one of the oldest centres of higher learning in the world, with an educational history dating back to the eighth century. Located in Tunis, the institution traces its origins to the Great Mosque of Ez-Zitouna, founded in 734 AD. According to the university’s official historical account, the teaching of Islamic sciences began there around 737 AD. Over the centuries, the institution became an important centre for Islamic scholarship, teaching subjects including Islamic jurisprudence, philosophy, mathematics, medicine and astronomy. It also attracted prominent scholars, including the renowned North African historian Ibn Khaldun, who studied at the institution. Ez-Zitouna remains an important institution for Islamic studies and is widely regarded as one of the oldest continuously operating educational traditions in the Arab and Islamic world. 2. Morocco – University of Al-Qarawiyyin (859 AD) Morocco is home to the University of Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, an institution widely recognised as the world’s oldest existing and continually operating educational institution. Founded in 859 AD, Al-Qarawiyyin was established as a mosque and centre of learning by Fatima al-Fihri, a Muslim woman who reportedly used her inheritance to finance its construction. The institution gradually developed into a major centre of Islamic scholarship, attracting students and scholars from different parts of Africa and beyond. Its academic activities historically covered Islamic theology, law, Arabic grammar, mathematics and astronomy, among other subjects. Al-Qarawiyyin’s historical significance extends beyond its age. Its establishment demonstrates the important role African women played in supporting education and intellectual development centuries ago. Today, the institution remains part of Morocco’s higher education system and continues to preserve its long-standing tradition of Islamic learning. 3. Egypt – Al-Azhar University (970 AD) Egypt is home to Al-Azhar University, another historic African institution that has played a significant role in global education and Islamic scholarship for more than 1,000 years. item.title: List of African countries that have their own unique calendars
item.description: Several African countries have calendars that are distinct from the Gregorian calendar, either because they maintain traditional systems of dating or because their religious and cultural communities follow their own calendars. The most notable example is Ethiopia, which has a separate calendar system used for official civil purposes. Other countries have indigenous or religious calendars that remain culturally significant, although they are not necessarily used for government administration. African countries with unique calendar systems 1. Ethiopia – Ethiopian (Ge’ez) Calendar Ethiopia operates a calendar that is approximately seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar. It has 13 months : 12 months of 30 days and a final month called Pagume, which has five or six days. Its New Year usually falls on September 11. 2. Egypt – Coptic Calendar The Coptic calendar descends from the ancient Egyptian calendar and is still used by the Coptic Orthodox Church. It has 13 months, with 12 months of 30 days and a short 13th month. Its New Year is known as Nayrouz. 3. Eritrea – Ge’ez Calendar Eritrean Orthodox Christians follow the Ge’ez calendar, which is closely related to Ethiopia’s calendar. Its New Year is called Kidus Yohannes and is celebrated around September 11. Eritrea uses the Gregorian calendar for official administration. 4. Morocco – Amazigh (Berber) Calendar The Amazigh calendar is used traditionally by Berber communities. It follows an agricultural year and marks its New Year, Yennayer, around January 12–14. Morocco recognises Yennayer as a public holiday. 5. Algeria – Amazigh Calendar Algeria also observes the Amazigh agricultural calendar. Yennayer marks the beginning of the traditional year and is celebrated as an important cultural occasion. 6. Nigeria – Igbo Traditional Calendar The Igbo calendar, known as Ọgụ́àfọ̀ Ị̀gbò, has 13 months in its traditional structure. Its week consists of four market days: Eke, Orie, Afọ and Nkwọ. It is used in traditional religious, cultural and market activities, although different Igbo communities may calculate it differently. 7. Ghana – Akan Calendar The Akan people use a traditional 42-day cycle known as Adaduanan, combining a six-day week and a seven-day week. It helps determine traditional festivals, ceremonies and important cultural events. Similar practices are found among Akan communities in Côte d’Ivoire. item.title: More than 900 US flights cancelled Sunday after Friday’s ground stop
item.description: …FAA expects flight schedules to recover by late Sunday By Juliet Umeh More than 900 flights scheduled for Sunday in the United States had been cancelled by late Saturday as airlines continued to recover from a nationwide ground stop imposed by the Federal Aviation Administration, FAA. FlightAware, a flight-tracking service, recorded 910 cancellations for Sunday, with the figure rising. More than 6,400 flights were cancelled on Saturday, following about 9,200 on Friday. The FAA order halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours on Friday. Although it was lifted that evening, passengers continued to face cancellations and delays as airlines worked to reposition aircraft and crews. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said, “I do think the worst is behind us,” but added that “a significant amount of recovery work” remained. He apologised to travellers, saying: “I’m sorry that we put you through this, but we did it for the right reasons.” US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the disruption began during work to replace old copper telecommunications lines with fibre-optic cables at an FAA facility. A router involved in the upgrade overloaded parts of the network, affecting air traffic communications and radar systems. “We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds,” Duffy said, adding that the surge caused “issues with our communication with airplanes” and disrupted radar feeds. Officials are investigating whether the problem resulted from an installation error or faulty equipment. “We haven’t determined what the fault was,” Duffy said. Bedford said airlines expected to restore their schedules by late Sunday. “Based on everything that we’re hearing from our airline partners, they believe that they’ll be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday,” he said. The FAA said it ordered the ground stop as a safety measure after communications problems affected 17 of its 22 en-route air traffic control centres. Bedford said, “No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost.” He also said there was “zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related.” The post More than 900 US flights cancelled Sunday after Friday’s ground stop appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NDLEA arrests American basketballer over 34kg cannabis consignment
item.description: Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) have intercepted a 25.05 kilograms consignment of methamphetamine at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos. The agency’s Director, Media and Advocacy, Mr Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday in Abuja. Babafemi said that the drugs were concealed in packs of assorted breakfast cereals imported from South Africa. He said that the NDLEA operatives arrested the 56-year-old trafficker who had lived in South Africa for over two decades under a stolen identity. He added that the meth suspect was arrested on Wednesday at the arrival hall of Terminal II of the Lagos airport upon his return from South Africa. “A thorough search of his two travelling boxes led to the recovery of twenty-five parcels of a white crystalline substance, which tested positive for methamphetamine with a total weight of 25.05kg. “The parcels had been carefully concealed inside packs of assorted breakfast cereals and cereal-based food products in a bid to beat security screening. “The 56-year-old suspect holds both Nigerian and South African passports and has been resident in South Africa for over 24 years. “During preliminary interview, he confessed that he adopted the fake Nigerian name after using forged documents to gain entry into South Africa and had continued to use that identity ever since. “He further stated that he was contracted by a South Africa-based man to deliver the illicit consignment in Nigeria for a fee of R20,000,”he said. Babafemi further disclosed that the agency’s operatives at the same airport, arrested an American professional basketball player over a 33.95kg shipment of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, from Thailand. Babafemi said that on Wednesday, acting on credible intelligence, NDLEA operatives at the MMIA intercepted a 28-year-old American citizen who arrived in Lagos aboard an Emirates Airline flight from Thailand via Dubai. He said that the suspect, who was placed under discreet surveillance upon arrival, was observed abandoning his two checked-in bags before attempting to exit the airport with only his carry-on luggage. “He was promptly apprehended at the airport car park. “A search of the two abandoned bags, both bearing his name tag, revealed sixteen parcels of Loud in each, totalling thirty-two parcels with a combined weight of 33.95 kilograms. “A tracking device was also recovered from the bags. The suspect, a native of Savannah, Georgia, USA, claimed he has lived in Thailand since October 2025 where he plays professional basketball. “The suspect said he came to Nigeria on holiday to build networks for his basketball career. “A forensic examination of his mobile phone revealed information pointing to his knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity,”he said The post NDLEA arrests American basketballer over 34kg cannabis consignment appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Revenue leakages: FG to deploy export automation system as non-oil sector hits over $6b
item.description: By Daniel Abia P/Harcourt The Federal Government has concluded the process to deploy an automated export processing system to strengthen regulatory compliance and curb revenue leakages in the exports sector. This was disclosed by, Mr Tola Fakolade, the Project Director, National Single Window (NSW), at the Phase Two Export Sensitization Joint Stakeholders Engagement in Port Harcourt on Thursday. The event had as its theme, “Unlocking Endless Possibilities: A Comprehensive Outlook on the NSW Project”. Fakolade described the NSW as a Federal Government initiative designed to streamline international trade through a unified digital platform for trade documentation, permits and approvals. “The second phase of the project, scheduled to commence on Dec. 14, is expected to eliminate the multiple bottlenecks, delays and revenue leakages that have long frustrated exporters,” he said. He said the first batch of the phase would cover the issuance of export permit issuance by agencies, including the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), NAFDAC and Federal Produce Inspection Service. According to him, the second batch, involving processes handled by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), would commence in the first quarter of 2027. Fakolade explained that the first phase had streamlined the submission of licences and permits by integrating the digital systems of various regulatory agencies. He said the platform had also strengthened compliance by ensuring that users met regulatory requirements before accessing relevant services. “One of the testimonials we received from agencies during the first phase was that enforced compliance on the platform helped users comply with regulations. “When there is compliance, there is also a reduction in revenue leakages,” he said. The NSW project director said the project team was engaging exporters and other stakeholders nationwide to ensure adequate awareness ahead of the second phase. He listed Enugu, Akure, Jos, Lagos and Port Harcourt among the cities already visited, adding that sensitisation would continue in Kano and Abuja. He said the NSW team was collaborating with the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC), which maintains the database of registered exporters. “The partnership would provide access to relevant information and insights required for effective implementation of the export phase,” he said. Fakolade said the project had completed its User Acceptance Testing and would commence end-user training on Monday. He urged exporters and other stakeholders to register for the training to familiarise themselves with the platform ahead of its implementation. item.title: Stop weaponising public for political relevance – Obi’s media office to Wike, Keyamo
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE Media Office of the Presidential Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC ahead of January 16 2027 election, Peter Obi has taken a swipe at the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory Administration, FCTA, Nyesom Wike and the Minister Nigeria’s Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, over attacks on the Presidential candidate over National anthem. In a statement signed on Sunday by the Spokesperson of Peter Obi Media Reach, POMR, Idris Zekeri, he described them as rabble rousers, warning them to stop weaponising public for political relevance. According to Zekeri, a government minister is not a political warlord and public office is neither a private arsenal nor are Nigeria’s state institutions extensions of any politician’s personal political organisation, urging Wike and Keyamo to recognise that they hold their offices in trust for Nigerians, not to serve political egos or protect partisan interests, adding that even more concerning is the attempt to portray partisan conduct as patriotism. The statement read, ” the Peter Obi Media Office strongly condemns the disturbing conduct of Ministers Nyesom Wike and Festus Keyamo, who appear to be exploiting their official positions for partisan political confrontation, treating the authority entrusted to them by Nigerians as though it were personal property to be deployed against political opponents. Their conduct raises a fundamental question: when did public service become an instrument for political intimidation, personal vendettas and the pursuit of narrow partisan interests? ” A government minister is not a political warlord. Public office is neither a private arsenal nor are Nigeria’s state institutions extensions of any politician’s personal political organisation. Wike and Keyamo must recognise that they hold their offices in trust for Nigerians, not to serve political egos or protect partisan interests. Even more concerning is the attempt to portray partisan conduct as patriotism. “Patriotism is not measured by the forcefulness of political rhetoric, the harshness of attacks on opponents or the unconditional defence of a government. It is demonstrated by service, integrity, respect for the rule of law and an unwavering commitment to the welfare of citizens. Claims of patriotism should be subjected to careful scrutiny rather than accepted without question. Nigerians must differentiate political antagonism from genuine patriotism and understand that loyalty to a political establishment is not equivalent to commitment to the nation. “No individual or political organisation has an exclusive monopoly on patriotism. item.title: Cabo Verde Votes In Presidential Election As Incumbent Seeks Second Term
item.description: Cabo Verde voted for a new president on Sunday, with incumbent Jose Maria Neves favoured to win a second term as head of state of the West African archipelago renowned for its democratic stability. He is facing the country’s first woman candidate, Joana Rosa Amado, among other contenders. Voting started at 0900 GMT and ends at 1900 GMT. Provisional results are expected overnight. “I’ve voted. Now I’m going to mass, and I believe everything will go well — normally and with civic-mindedness,” Adilia Gomes, 55, told AFP after casting her ballot in the capital, Praia. “Everything went normally despite a few minutes’ delay in the opening of my polling station,” added another voter, Claudino Semedo. Nearly 420,000 people are eligible to vote. The election is being watched by about 150 observers from the Economic Community of West African States, the African Union and European Union. A supporter of Cape Verde’s President and presidential candidate Jose Maria Neves waves a flag bearing his image during a campaign rally in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on October 30, 2026.(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) Cabo Verde, located in the Atlantic Ocean about 600 kilometres (375 miles) off the coast of Senegal, comprises 10 volcanic islands and is an increasingly popular tourist destination. It made world headlines this year when its national football team reached the knockout stages in its first World Cup, and when a cruise ship containing people with hantavirus docked off its shores. Stability, Hospitality Unlike several of its West African neighbours where presidential elections have been tense in recent years, Cabo Verde is known for its political stability and good governance. It is considered a model of democracy in Africa, with strong economic growth. A voter queues at a polling station during Cape Verde’s presidential election in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on November 15, 2026(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) The country is known for its “morabeza” (“hospitality”, in local creole), openness, and carnivals. It also has its own style of music. According to the Mo Ibrahim Foundation 2026 index on global governance, Cabo Verde ranks third out of 54 countries on the continent. Politically, it has a semi-presidential system in which the executive is dominated by the prime minister. The president does not govern but acts more as an arbiter, working to guarantee unity and uphold the constitution. The head of state appoints the prime minister based on the results of legislative elections and represents the country abroad. item.title: Meta fined €805m for accessing users’ photos, videos without consent
item.description: Italian regulators fined Facebook parent company Meta 805 million euros ($880 million) for accessing users’ photos without their “specific” consent, the country’s data protection authority said on Saturday. Through the Facebook application for Android devices, Meta accessed photographs, videos and related metadata belonging to Italian users “without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them”, the authority said in a statement. Meta said it would appeal the decision. A company spokesperson said “we strongly disagree” with the assessment by the regulators “and the disproportionate level of the fine”. In late October, authorities in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for having misled the state’s residents for more than a decade over use of their data — a record fine for the company, which slammed it as a “tax” on freedom of expression. Saturday’s latest fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant. In 2021, Amazon received a more than 1.1-billion-euro fine for breaching competition law. That sum was subsequently reduced to 752 million euros on appeal. – Facebook gallery feature – The Italian penalty imposed on Facebook relates to its gallery suggestions feature, available since 2023, which suggests photos and videos from a user’s phone gallery as ideas for posts as they are browsing. According to Italy’s regulator, Facebook requested access to the gallery via a single authorisation valid for the entire app, preceded by a generic notice requesting enabling of other features, which did not allow users to understand that they were also authorising suggestions from their gallery. The regulator said Meta would now have to seek consent by means of a separate and specific request for the feature concerned and clearly signpost what it is used for, namely that it involves access to a user’s photo gallery, as well as how to disable it. In determining the size of the fine, the authority said it took into account “the high number of people affected” — around 20 million Android users in Italy — and the duration of the infringement, “which is still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system”. The authority also cited “Meta’s lack of cooperation during the investigation”. It imposed a fine amounting to roughly 0.4 per cent of the group’s annual turnover, which hit $201 billion in 2025, for a net profit of $60.5 billion. item.description: . Rejects Appeal Court ruling on PDP leadership crisis . Wabara, who expressed strong reservations over the recent Court of Appeal judgment in the PDP leadership dispute, accused the ruling party of benefiting from the protracted crises in opposition parties and warned that attempts to weaken political alternatives ahead of the 2027 general elections could undermine Nigeria’s democratic foundations. He described the appellate court’s refusal to compel the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise his faction’s position as a travesty of justice, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the emergence of the Alhaji Abdulrahman Muhammad-led faction raised serious questions about democracy in Nigeria. The former Senate President warned that accepting the Muhammad-led faction’s position without adequately addressing the issues surrounding its emergence amounted to “standing truth in the head”. The Court of Appeal, in a unanimous decision by a three-member panel, had declined to disturb the July 17, 2026 judgment of the Federal High Court in Abuja, which dismissed the suit filed by the Wabara-led BoT faction. Those actions included a national convention organised by the faction, which subsequently announced former President Goodluck Jonathan as its consensus presidential candidate for the 2027 election. In the lead judgment delivered virtually by Justice R. O. Ayoola, the appellate court held that the Wabara-led group lacked the locus standi to institute the action on behalf of the PDP. Reacting to the judgment, Wabara expressed bewilderment at what he described as its questionable legal reasoning, wondering how the appellate court arrived at what he called an inverted interpretation of the issues before it. He cautioned the judiciary against becoming entangled in political disputes in ways that could further erode public confidence in the institution. item.title: Talent without principles can lead you astray, Rwandan author warns
item.description: Rwandan author, Lisa Munezero, has warned that people with talent but no principles can go astray, saying fulfilling one’s purpose requires integrity and uprightness. Munezero also said Rwanda’s post-genocide generation needs healing, adding that her book, titled: ‘The Well of Knowing’, seeks to contribute to that process. The business expert spoke at the book’s launch in Lagos, where she said the publication seeks to change how the world sees Africa. She said: “Whatever you are good at, any talent you have, but if you don’t have principles in your life, if you don’t know how to set boundaries, if you don’t know what you should do, what you have to avoid, you always find yourself in a place where you shouldn’t be. Everyone should know their purpose. Even for Christians, the Bible says, it’s not something people created. It’s something that even God created us to fill. There is a space we have to fill in this life. Purpose tells you why.” On how she started writing, she said: “My journey to write started when I was a little girl. When it started, I can say it was in a form of healing. In Rwanda in 1994, there was a genocide against the Tutsi. I was born after the genocide. I grew up in a society where it started from zero. Families, government, everyone. As far as I remember, when I was in primary school, I used to write. I liked to write. In 2017, I wanted to write a book. “I used to write some stories. Different things related to content of healing, reconciliation, like other students. I had the privilege to write about how people like me, young generation, who were born after the genocide, came here. We needed to heal too. We grew up in a family that lost so many people. Others were in jail. Some students used to say that fathers of family members are dead because of what they did. They feel ashamed. It was a challenge to me. After that, because I used to love to write, I found out that I’m a good writer because when I used to write, to teach, people used to come to me and say, I feel my life has changed. “Wherever I am, I want to show that I’m from Africa. I want people to respect Africa as much as they respect other people from other continents. I chose to write something that I live in my life. My experience, my background, and African stories. In this book, there is testimony of Africa. I chose to go that way.” Also speaking at the event, one of the book’s reviewers, Adekunle Adekenambi, said that, unlike many other books, ‘The Well of Knowing’ contains several examples drawn from African experiences. According to him, everyone interested in living a successful life, running a successful business or leading a successful family or administration should read the book. He said: “As a father, I picked something from the book. Do not force your child to do anything. item.title: Two dead as car fleeing police crashes in UK
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Two people have died after a car being pursued by police collided with their vehicle in Leeds, a city in West Yorkshire in northern England, UK. According to a report, West Yorkshire Police said a blue BMW 123D “failed to stop” for a police vehicle on Gelderd Road at 12:44 a.m. on Sunday. Officers began a pursuit, during which the BMW collided with a white Volkswagen Scirocco turning into Gelderd Road from Lowfields Road. The media report said that the driver of the Volkswagen, a 22-year-old man from York, died at the scene. It said: “His passenger, a 23-year-old woman, also from York, died in hospital a short time later. “A 39-year-old man from Harrogate, who was in the BMW, was arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and driving while over the prescribed limit for cannabis. He remains in custody. “Three other occupants of the BMW – two boys aged 16 and 17, and a 16-year-old girl – were taken to hospital with injuries police said were not life-threatening. They have also been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving. “The Independent Office for Police Conduct has declared an independent investigation after a referral from West Yorkshire Police. “Gelderd Road remained closed, with drivers advised to avoid the area and use alternative routes,” the report added. item.title: Nigeria, Saudi Arabia to begin direct Abuja-Jeddah flights in December, says envoy
item.description: Nigeria and Saudi Arabia are set to strengthen their air connectivity, with Saudi Arabia’s national carrier, Saudia Airlines, scheduled to begin direct flights between Abuja and Jeddah in December. Nigerian Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Dr Yakubu Gambo, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria on Sunday. Gambo said the service would subsequently extend to Lagos and Port Harcourt. He said Kano would retain its existing direct flight arrangement, while additional routes were expected to be operational before the end of the first quarter of 2027. “By December, we will start having Saudi air flights directly from Abuja. And it will scale up to Lagos, Port Harcourt and Kano,” he said. Gambo said the arrangement followed adjustments and engagements with Saudi aviation authorities, who expressed willingness to support direct air connectivity between both countries. He said Saudi Arabia had also indicated readiness to provide technical and financial support for Nigeria to operate flights through its national carrier. According to him, the arrangement will enable Nigerian pilgrims travelling for Hajj and Umrah to fly directly between both countries without transiting through other territories. “They wouldn’t want pilgrims coming for Umrah or Hajj to fly through other territories that may not be safe,” he said. The ambassador said President Bola Tinubu had been briefed on the proposal and welcomed the initiative. He confirmed that direct flights would also be available for Nigerian pilgrims during the 2027 Hajj exercise. Travis Barker, the drummer from Blink-182, inducted Collins, drawing tears from the British artist who attended the ceremony alongside his children, including Lily of “Emily in Paris” fame. item.title: 2027: SERAP Gives INEC Seven Days To Prosecute Electoral Violence Suspects
item.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has given the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) seven days to prosecute persons arrested over reported incidents of electoral and political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections or face legal action. SERAP made the demand in a letter dated November 14, 2026, and addressed to INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, urging the commission to obtain relevant case files and investigation materials from the Nigeria Police Force and prosecute suspects where sufficient evidence exists. The organisation also asked INEC to direct its legal officers or appointed legal practitioners to review the files and promptly initiate prosecutions under the Electoral Act 2026. The demand follows several reported incidents of political violence across the country since campaigns for the 2027 elections began on 19 August, including the latest attack on members and supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in Oregun, Lagos, on 12 November. In the letter signed by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Oluwadare, SERAP urged Amupitan to press the police to conclude investigations into other reported attacks, arrest suspected perpetrators and their sponsors, and forward relevant evidence to INEC. It also called on the commission to exercise its powers under Section 83 of the Electoral Act 2026 to demand explanations from political parties suspected of involvement in or encouraging prohibited conduct and impose prescribed fines on those that fail to comply with lawful directives. SERAP expressed concern over reports of attacks on political convoys, party secretariats, rallies and meetings, as well as intimidation of candidates and supporters. Cited incidents included the reported obstruction of the convoy of NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi in Benue State on 8 September; attacks on political meetings in Enugu State on 12 September; and the attack on the convoy of ADC senatorial candidate Herberta Okonofua in Edo State on 6 October. Others included attacks on supporters of Accord governorship candidate Oriyomi Hamzat in Ibadan on 14 October, which reportedly resulted in one death, and the attack on the convoy of NDC candidate Rollins Offia-Nwali in Ebonyi State on 22 October, which allegedly left one person dead and three injured. The organisation also cited the reported attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore and his team in Ado-Ekiti on 30 October, the attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar on 4 November, and an NDC procession in Asaba on 7 November, which reportedly left one person dead and five injured. It added that journalist Samuel Adebanjo was assaulted and his equipment seized while covering the November 12 incident in Lagos. item.title: [VIDEO] Taraba Records 72 Road Crash Deaths In 10 Months – FRSC
item.description: No fewer than 72 people died in 115 road traffic crashes recorded in Taraba State between January and October 2026, the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has said. The FRSC Sector Commander in Taraba, Anna Attah, disclosed this during a press briefing in Jalingo to mark the 2026 World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims.
